content.title: About
content.content: Stew, fish is a dish made from fish slowly simmered in a sauce of vegetables, spices, and sometimes wine. The gentle cooking preserves the delicate flavor of the fish while creating a tender texture and a broth rich in vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fish stew is popular in Mediterranean, Asian, and Scandinavian cuisines.
Traditional preparation uses low heat in clay pots or covered pans.
Different fish species (cod, salmon, pike) give distinct flavor notes.
Adding tomatoes, lemon juice, or wine enhances aroma and antioxidant content.
Fish stew is often served with whole grains, potatoes, or fresh herbs.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Fish provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Stewed fish, especially from fatty varieties, supplies EPA and DHA, supporting heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish retains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Fish is abundant in iodine, selenium, and phosphorus, which aid thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with modest oil, the stew remains heart‑friendly.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions, ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Contaminant risk
items.content: Certain fish can contain mercury or other toxins; choose small‑to‑medium species from reputable sources.

items.title: Overcooking
items.content: Excessive simmering can make the fish dry and harder to digest.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Broths often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stew hot with its sauce alongside a side such as mashed potatoes, rice, couscous, or fresh vegetables. Garnish with herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or capers for brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers in an airtight container and refrigerate for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze up to 3 months after fully cooling and portioning.
